label: non-i token right after an early "i i" pair in the original sequence
explanation: Sparse feature (0.04% of steps) that fires almost only in the original-input phase (93% of mass) at early positions t=2-5 (t=0,1 never; nearly nothing after t=6). The dominant factor is that the previous input was the letter i (68% of mass, 23x lift), with w a weaker alternative (15% of mass). The strongest activations come on the first non-i token after a doubled "i i" near the start, e.g. j i i [l], s i i [d], f i i i [f]. Magnitude also depends on the current token: f, l, d, 3, y, c and q give larger values. Weaker activations follow a single i or w (r i [y], j d i w [q]). Rare small activations appear at the delimiter and the first copy steps. It does not fire on i itself, at t<2, late in the sequence, or after most other tokens. Even so, prev_tok==i at an early position has only about 3% precision, so the feature reads as a soft conjunction of early position, recent i, and the identity of the current token. The recorded predicate (i i then a non-i token at t=2-4) has the best F1 (dev 0.35, precision 0.46) but covers only about a third of the activation mass.
